_purpose: Decision data for `mcgyvr init`: given detected hardware, propose worker bindings without benchmarking the user's machine. Every number here is measured, not estimated, and carries its provenance. See data/README.md for methodology and known-bad measurements.

quality_metric.name: humaneval_plus_pass1
quality_metric._caveat: Coding-benchmark pass@1 is a proxy for worker suitability, not a promise about a user's repo. It ranks models; it does not predict acceptance rate on real contracts.

harness_caveats.summary: Ollama /api/generate yields invalid HumanEval+ scores for Qwen2.5-Coder 7B and larger.
harness_caveats.detail: Measured 32.3% (7b) and 17.1% (14b) via ollama /api/generate; the same weights via llama-server scored 84.1% and 87.8% — deltas of +54.9pp and +73.8pp. Non-Qwen models (yi-coder, deepseek-coder-v2) scored correctly through the same ollama path.
harness_caveats.consequence: Any capability data collected through ollama /api/generate for these models must be discarded. A table built from them would systematically under-route to the best available local models.

harness_caveats.summary: Ollama resolves qwen3-coder-30b-a3b to an F16 weight set (~18 GB), not a Q4 quant.
harness_caveats.detail: The F16 pull spills ~59% to CPU on a 12 GB card, runs ~100 s/task and scores 3.7%. The same model as a Q2_K GGUF under llama-server scores 87.8% in ~3 GB.
harness_caveats.consequence: MoE models of this family must be bound to an explicit GGUF quant under llama-server, never left to ollama tag resolution.

harness_caveats.summary: The gpt-oss-20b score below is disputed and should not be used for routing.
harness_caveats.detail: Originally attributed to MXFP4 quantization destroying code quality. Later investigation attributed the failure to an insufficient output token budget in the harness, not to the quantization.
harness_caveats.consequence: Treat gpt-oss-20b as unmeasured until re-run. Do not propose it, and do not cite 53.7% as its quality.

harness_caveats.summary: A model that fits VRAM only marginally thrashes rather than failing.
harness_caveats.detail: qwen2.5-coder:7b (~5 GB) on a 6 GB card ran at 30.4 tok/s against 57.6 tok/s on a 12 GB card — a 1.9x penalty from a card with 2.5x fewer cores, indicating memory pressure rather than compute limits.
harness_caveats.consequence: Propose a binding only where the model's footprint leaves headroom for KV cache; marginal fits are a worse experience than the tier below.

models.notes: Fastest option on a small card and by a wide margin. Quality is the floor of what is useful; suits mechanical, tightly-scoped contracts.
Best quality-per-GB below 6 GB. The 1.5B→3B step is +15.3pp HumanEval+; the 3B→7B step is +2.4pp on the same rig.
Needs ≥8 GB to run without memory pressure.
Highest measured dense-model quality. Needs ≥12 GB.
Dominated by qwen2.5-coder:7b — smaller, faster and 15pp better. Present for completeness.
Fastest large model measured, but 15pp below qwen2.5-coder:14b at a similar footprint. A throughput lane, never a quality rung — binding it above 7B inverts the quality gradient.

Highest quality per GB measured: 14B-class quality in ~3 GB. Slow, and requires an explicit GGUF quant under llama-server. Strong fit for a quality rung on a small card where latency is not the constraint.
Quality unmeasured pending a re-run with an adequate output budget. Not proposed.

concurrency_findings.summary: Distinct models run genuinely concurrently on one GPU.
concurrency_findings.detail: Three models (1.5B + 3B + 16B MoE) completed in 23.6 s wall against ~44 s serial, each holding its solo throughput, at 11.8 GB total on a 12 GB card.

concurrency_findings.summary: Same-model concurrency scales 1.6–3.1x with server-side parallelism enabled.
concurrency_findings.detail: Requires the backend's parallel-slot setting; a single-slot server serializes same-model requests.

concurrency_findings.summary: Aggregate throughput across separate machines degrades 0–15%.
concurrency_findings.detail: Separate GPUs share no bus; a pool spanning hosts is close to additive.
